What to Write in an Apology Letter: A Sincere Step-by-Step Guide

Learn what to write in an apology letter to a partner, friend or family member, with a structure for accountability, empathy and meaningful repair.

An apology letter can help you slow down and choose your words carefully. It is most useful when it explains what happened, acknowledges the impact and describes a realistic step toward repair. It should not demand forgiveness or make the recipient responsible for your guilt.

Communication & Repair8 min readUpdated 7 November 2026
Written by RA FahimWishly Guide Editorial

Open by naming the issue

Start with a clear sentence about what you are apologising for. Avoid vague openings that make the recipient work out what you mean. If you are unsure about a detail, do not invent it; ask for clarification before writing.

A specific opening demonstrates that you are addressing the actual concern rather than sending a general message to end discomfort.

Acknowledge the other person’s experience

Describe the impact you understand your actions had. Do not tell the recipient how they should feel. Use language such as “I can see that this put you in a difficult position” or “I understand why that broke your trust.”

If you do not yet understand the impact, acknowledge that and invite them to explain when they are ready. Listening is part of the apology process.

Take responsibility without excuses

Use direct language about your choices. You may provide context, but do not use it to cancel responsibility or shift blame. Avoid “I am sorry, but…” and “I am sorry you took it that way.”

A sincere apology is not a negotiation. You can own your part even if there are other issues to discuss later. Keep those conversations separate so that the apology remains clear.

Advertisements

Describe what will change

Offer one or two realistic actions. Explain how you will avoid repeating the behaviour, correct a mistake or respect a boundary. Do not make promises you cannot control.

If the issue involves a pattern, change takes time. Follow through consistently and let the recipient evaluate the change rather than asking them to reassure you immediately.

Close without demanding forgiveness

End with gratitude for reading, an invitation to talk if they want and respect for their timing. The recipient is allowed to need space or choose not to continue the relationship.

Wishly’s Sorry Letter or Premium Sorry templates can present your message in a thoughtful format. Use the design only when receiving a digital letter would be welcome; do not send it after someone has asked for no contact.

Frequently asked questions

How long should an apology letter be?

Keep it long enough to be specific and accountable, but avoid repeating the same point or making the recipient comfort you.

Should an apology letter include an excuse?

Context may be relevant, but it should not be used to cancel responsibility or blame the recipient.

Can I send an apology letter online?

Yes, if digital contact is welcome. A personal letter webpage can help organise the message, but respect boundaries.
